Naming — what does this control expose?

Names and descriptions are read from the accessibility tree. That proves exposure, never announcement — what a screen reader does with a string is product-dependent and is not claimed here.
The plain-CSS layer cannot produce ARIA, so what it ships is a markup convention: a hint carries id="<control-id>-hint", an error carries id="<control-id>-error", and the control lists them in aria-describedby in reading order. The React layer wires the same relationship by construction in FormControl. scripts/__tests__/input-specimens.node.mjs enforces the convention across this whole page, so it is a rule rather than two hand-wired specimens.

Visible label
expects: name "Project name" — the case the markup uses
Placeholder as a format hint
expects: name "Search projects" from the hidden label; the placeholder shows the format and is never the name. Before this rung existed the control was named "Search projects…" by its placeholder alone — which axe lists under passes, and which disappears the moment the user types.
aria-label only
expects: name "Filter results"
Hidden label
expects: name "Filter results", and the label occupies no layout space
aria-label on an icon-only controlexpects: the one rung where aria-label is sanctioned: there is no text to label, and the glyph carries no name of its own
Hidden until focusedSkip to the end of this sectionTab to it — it takes layout space only while focused.expects: the skip-link case: hidden at rest, visible on focus, named throughout
Group legend
Retention policy
expects: group name "Retention policy"
Help text
Must be reachable over HTTPS.
expects: description contains "Must be reachable over HTTPS."
Error text
That address did not resolve. Check the host, then try again.
expects: description contains the error copy, and aria-invalid is true
Help plus error
Whole days, 1 or more.Zero is not a window. Enter 1 or more days.
expects: description contains each message exactly once
Required marker
expects: name "Retention required", required true, and no marker glyph in the name

Focus — does the ring survive the page around it?

The global ring is delivered by a zero-specificity :where() rule as a box-shadow. Any author box-shadow at class specificity or above replaces it, with no error and no gate.

Select chrome — the chevron guard

Permanent guard for the background-shorthand regression: a shorthand resets background-image, -repeat, -position and -size, which deleted the chevron in light and tiled it across the whole control in dark.
